sections.label: Fire deaths and safety breaches
sections.summary: The fire killed 72 people, destroyed 151 homes and left over 200 homeless, while experts found non-compliant fire doors and cladding.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: The fire claimed 72 lives, destroyed 151 homes and rendered more than 200 residents homeless.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: While the inquiry is still ongoing, fire safety experts have discovered many serious fire safety breaches, such as the installation of over 100 non-compliant fire doors and the use of non-compliant external cladding, which contributed to the tragedy.

sections.label: Singapore fire fatality rate
sections.summary: Singapore's fire fatality rate fell by half from 0.15 per 100,000 in 2014 to 0.07 in 2018, and remains low compared with other cities.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: In Singapore, our fire fatality rate remains low, as compared with cities, such as Hong Kong, London, New York and Tokyo.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: We have succeeded in reducing it by half from 0.15 fatalities per 100,000 population in 2014, to 0.07 in 2018.

sections.label: Review of Fire Safety Act
sections.summary: Taller, denser buildings and new materials prompted a review of the Act, and the amendment Bill has five thrusts.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Indeed, in recent years, we have observed developments which give impetus to bringing the Act up to date, among others: (a) an increase in the height of buildings and urban density in Singapore, which makes firefighting operations even more challenging, as well as increase the potential damage from fires; and (b) the introduction of new building materials and products, which may pose higher fire risks.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: We have, therefore, reviewed the Act, and the amendment Bill will have the following thrusts: one, to enhance the fire safety of buildings in Singapore; two, to increase the accountability of all parties involved in the supply chain for regulated fire safety products; three, to enhance SCDF’s investigative and enforcement powers to prevent and rectify non-compliances; four, to optimise SCDF’s capabilities and resources by allowing them to focus on the areas which present higher fire safety risks, and outsource more routine and straightforward functions; and five, to provide greater clarity to the industry on fire safety standards.

sections.label: Tightening cladding supply chain
sections.summary: SCDF found the external cladding composite panels were non-compliant, contributing to the fire's rapid spread, so controls over the supply chain will be tightened.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: To do so, we will tighten controls over the entire supply chain.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: SCDF’s investigations found that the composite panels used as the building’s external cladding were not compliant with the required standards, which contributed to the rapid spread of the fire.

sections.label: Offences for non-compliant products
sections.summary: Clause 26 inserts a new Part Five creating offences for supplying non-compliant products, false test reports and false certification, and powers to recall products.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Clause 26, therefore, inserts a new Part Five on regulated fire safety products, which will introduce enforcement levers over all actors in the supply chain: (a) the new section 32C makes it an offence for any person to supply a non-compliant fire safety product; (b) the new section 32 makes it an offence for any test laboratory to issue a false test report; (c) the new section 32B makes it an offence for any person who is not an accredited certification body to certify these products and for accredited certification bodies to falsely issue a certificate of conformity; and (d) when non-compliant products find their way into the market or into our buildings, the new section 33A empowers the Commissioner to issue directions to any party with possession, charge or control of the product to recall, cease supply, remove or dispose of the product, as well as to rectify any contravention.

sections.label: Cancelling certificates of conformity
sections.summary: The new section 33B lets the Commissioner order a certification body to cancel existing certificates of conformity in specified cases.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: If the certification body falsely issues a CoC or does not cancel the CoC after knowing that the product does not meet the applicable standards, or if the party refuses to comply with SCDF’s order to test the product, the new section 33B allows the Commissioner to order the certification body to cancel any existing CoCs.

sections.label: Fire hazard offences
sections.summary: Sections 12A and 12B create offences for causing fire hazards, faulty fire safety measures or obstructed escape routes.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Section 12A will make it an offence for building owners or occupiers to cause or fail to abate or prevent these fire hazards and section 12B will make it an offence for any responsible party to cause any fire safety measure in the premises to not be in proper working order or to cause an obstruction of fire escape routes.

sections.label: Powers to examine persons
sections.summary: Clause 7 inserts section 8CA empowering the Commissioner or authorised SCDF member to examine persons for investigations.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Clause 7 inserts a new section 8CA, which empowers the Commissioner or an authorised SCDF member to examine persons and require them to attend before SCDF for investigations into any offences under the Act.

sections.label: Higher penalties for Registered Inspectors
sections.summary: Penalties for a Registered Inspector who fails to inspect and verify fire safety works rise to $100,000 and/or two years' jail.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: For example, the penalties for an appointed Registered Inspector who fails to inspect and verify that fire safety works have been completed according to approved plans will be increased from a current maximum fine of $10,000 and/or six months' jail term, to a maximum fine of $100,000 and/or two years' jail term.

sections.label: Third-party officers appointed
sections.summary: SCDF is looking to appoint a small team of around five third-party officers to conduct these tasks.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: For a start, SCDF is looking to appoint a small team of around five third-party officers to conduct these tasks.

sections.label: Alarm monitoring licensing and Fire Certificates
sections.summary: Clause 17 inserts Part IIIB licensing alarm monitoring services, and clause 10 requires designated buildings to have a Fire Certificate.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Given the important role of alarm operators, as well as the projected 2% to 3% annual increase in demand for such services, clause 17 inserts a new Part IIIB on the licensing of persons providing alarm monitoring services.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: This will allow SCDF to regulate the operators, set minimum service standards and ensure service continuity.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Clause 10 repeals and inserts a new section 20, which requires designated buildings or classes of buildings to have a Fire Certificate in order to be occupied or used.

sections.label: Fire Code definition amended
sections.summary: The definition of the Fire Code will be amended to make clear the version on SCDF's website is the latest.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: For example, the definition of the Fire Code will be amended to make clear that the current version published on SCDF's website is the latest version.

sections.label: Fire hazards direct offence
sections.summary: New sections 12A and 12B in clause 9 make specified fire hazards a direct offence instead of requiring a notice first.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: New sections 12A and 12B in clause 9 makes specified fire hazards a direct offence instead of needing a notice to be issued as a preamble to an offence.

sections.label: SCDF notices for fire safety
sections.summary: Clause 10 lets SCDF issue notices to building owners to provide or install fire safety measures even without renovations if necessary for public safety.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Clause 10 of the Bill allows the SCDF to issue notices to building owners to provide or install fire safety measures even if they are not going through renovations if they are of the view that it is necessary for public safety.

sections.label: Public building definition amended
sections.summary: Clause 2(g) amends the meaning of public building from building purposes to whether the public has access.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Additionally, the meaning of "public building" is amended in clause 2(g) from a definition that focuses on the purposes of the building to whether or not "the public or a section of the public has access as of right, or by virtue of express or implied permission with or without payment of a fee".

sections.label: Alarm monitoring services regulated
sections.summary: Clause 17 inserts Part IIIB of the Act, which regulates alarm monitoring services.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Clause 17 of this Bill inserts Part IIIB of the Act which regulates alarm monitoring services.

sections.label: PAB and PMD fires rise
sections.summary: Fires caused by Power-Assisted Bicycles and Personal Mobility Devices increased significantly, with 54 reported in the first six months of this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: In recent months, the number of fires caused by Power-Assisted Bicycles (PABs) and Personal Mobility Devices (PMDs) have increased significantly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: There were 54 such reported fires in the first six months of this year.

sections.label: Fire injuries and fires compared
sections.summary: Thirty-one people were injured in 36 fires versus 11 people in 23 fires at the beginning of last year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Thirty-one people were injured in 36 fires versus 11 people in 23 fires in the beginning of last year.

sections.label: PMD fires and registered scooters
sections.summary: PMD-caused fires need firefighting resources and have cost families homes, property, pets and loved ones, with over 85,000 e-scooters registered at end June.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: These	fires	caused	by	PMDs	often	need	firefighting resources and have robbed many a family of their home, property, pets and even a loved one.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: There were more than 85,000 electric scooters registered at the end of June.

sections.label: Removing non-compliant external cladding
sections.summary: SCDF identified and ordered some buildings to remove external cladding that did not meet fire safety requirements.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: SCDF also identified and ordered some buildings to remove external cladding that did not meet fire safety requirements.

sections.label: Old buildings fire safety upgrades
sections.summary: SCDF has identified some 500 old buildings to undergo critical fire safety upgrades necessary for public safety.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: SCDF has identified some 500 old buildings to undergo critical fire safety upgrades necessary for public safety.

sections.label: PMD fires, agencies, UL2272 compliance
sections.summary: First half year saw 49 fires and one death; the speaker hopes agencies act together and notes MOT will bring forward UL2272 compliance to 1 July next year.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: First half year, 49 fires, one death and it is still counting.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I hope multi-agencies, SCDF, MOT, HDB and even the Ministry of Education (MOE) could come together and take bold and decisive action.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I am glad to hear from the Ministerial Statement just now that MOT will bring forward the compliance of UL2272 PMDs to 1 July next year, but this does not mean there will be no fire incidents.

sections.label: Third-party fire inspectors with body cameras
sections.summary: SCDF will train third-party fire inspectors, mostly Auxiliary Police and retired Home Team personnel, who will wear body cameras so SCDF can evaluate their work.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: To inspect more buildings, SCDF will train third-party fire inspectors.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: These inspectors will wear a body camera at work so that SCDF can evaluate whether their work is up to standard.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: These inspectors are mostly Auxiliary Police and retired Home Team personnel.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: There were 49 PMD-related fires in the first half of this year.

sections.label: Implementing fire safety standard quickly
sections.summary: The fire safety standard should be implemented as soon as possible, and best if it can be implemented right away.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The fire safety standard should be implemented as soon as possible, and best if it can be implemented right away.

sections.label: SCDF Commissioner fire safety upgrade powers
sections.summary: Proposed section 20A empowers the SCDF Commissioner to mandate building owners to install critical fire safety upgrades.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Under the proposed section 20A of the Act, the Commissioner of SCDF will be empowered to mandate building owners to install critical fire safety upgrades.

sections.label: Buildings identified by Senior Parliamentary Secretary
sections.summary: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary said about 500 such buildings have been identified.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary also mentioned earlier that about 500 such buildings have been identified.

sections.label: Fire Safety Certificate and cladding notices
sections.summary: SCDF issued a Fire Safety Certificate before occupation, then later issued notices to owners of over 40 buildings that their claddings were non-compliant.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: It was only thereafter that SCDF would issue a Fire Safety Certificate, allowing the premises to be occupied.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: It was thus surprising that in the months thereafter, SCDF issued notices to owners of more than 40 buildings that their claddings were non-compliant with the Fire Code.

sections.label: SCDF cladding investigations and charges
sections.summary: In the Toh Guan incident, the cladding supplier and its marketing manager were charged with cheating, and SCDF cited buildings with non-compliant cladding for replacement.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Regarding SCDF’s investigations into the cladding cases, I note that for the Toh Guan incident, the cladding supplier and its marketing manager have been charged in Court with several counts of cheating and the case is pending before the Courts.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In cases where Fire Safety Certificates were issued by SCDF before occupation, these parties would also have relied on the certificates to assume they were compliant.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: SCDF subsequently cited these buildings for having non-compliant cladding, requiring replacement with compliant materials.

sections.label: Third-party enforcement officers appointment
sections.summary: Proposed section 8F allows the Commissioner SCDF to appoint third-party enforcement officers for routine fire safety checks and building inspections.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Under the proposed section 8F, the Commissioner SCDF can appoint third-party enforcement officers to do routine fire safety enforcement checks and building inspections.

sections.label: Size of third-party officer force
sections.summary: The passage asks how large a force of third-party officers SCDF expects to maintain at steady state.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: At the steady state, how large a force of third-party officers does SCDF expect to maintain?

sections.label: Singapore fire rates 2013-2017
sections.summary: From 2013 to 2017, Singapore averaged 0.76 fires per 1,000 people, lower than the average of about two per 1,000.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: From 2013-2017, Singapore reported an average of 0.76 fires per 1,000 people, significantly lower than the average of about two per 1,000.

sections.label: Mandating HDB home fire alarm devices
sections.summary: The speaker proposes the Government mandate all HDB flats install home fire alarm devices, with initial installation costs in existing flats paid by the Government.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: But I want to highlight an area where we can do more.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I propose that with the powers under this Bill, the Government mandate that all HDB flats install home fire alarm devices (HFADs), with the initial installation costs in existing HDB flats to be paid for by the Government.

sections.label: Estimated programme cost of HFADs
sections.summary: Assuming upper-end costs, the programme could cost about $80 million for equipment, perhaps that again for installation and public education, totalling maybe $160 million.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: If we assume the cost to be on the upper end of this, we are looking at a programme cost of about $80 million for equipment, perhaps that amount again for installation costs, and public education, for a total of maybe $160 million.

sections.label: Smoke alarm study on fire deaths
sections.summary: A 2016 Fire Safety Journal paper found homes with working HFADs had half the fire death rates of homes without working devices.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In a recent paper titled "The association between smoke alarm presence and injury and death rates: A systematic review and meta-analysis", published in the Fire Safety Journal in 2016, researchers found that homes with working HFADs had half the death rates from fire compared to homes without working devices.

sections.label: Salesmen falsely claiming authority
sections.summary: Some salesmen falsely claimed to be agents of SCDF, the local Member of Parliament or other authorities, and equipment may be sold at grossly marked up prices.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Some of these salesmen have falsely claimed to be agents of SCDF, the local Member of Parliament or other authorities.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The equipment may be sold at grossly marked up prices.

sections.label: Mandating HFADs in HDB flats
sections.summary: The speaker says private property support should also be considered for mandating installation, and that the Bill's powers should mandate all HDB flats install HFADs, with public funds paying the first installation round.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Of course, if we can work out a plan for supporting private property owners, we should also consider mandating installation in all residential private property, to make the nation fire safe.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We should use the powers under this Bill to mandate that all HDB flats install HFADs, and to ensure that installation rates are high, we should use public funds to pay for the first round of installation.

sections.label: Residential fire injuries and death
sections.summary: Injuries in residential fires rose to 31 in the first half of 2019 from 11 in 2018, and a 41-year-old man died in July after a Bukit Batok HDB flat fire.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The number of people injured in such fires in residential premises increased to 31 in the first half of 2019 compared to 11 in the first half of 2018.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: A 41-year-old man died recently in July after being rescued from such a fire in a Bukit Batok HDB flat in the wee hours of the night.

sections.label: Smoke detector and HFAD installation
sections.summary: The Ministry mandated HFADs in all new residential homes including HDB flats from June 2018 and is retrofitting HFADs free for 50,000 needy public rental households.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: However, at the same time, the Ministry has acknowledged it is important to install smoke detectors in residential buildings and has mandated the installation of HFADs in all new residential homes, including HDB flats from June 2018.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: There is also an exercise to retrofit HFADs to benefit 50,000 needy households in public rental flats for free.

sections.label: Ang Mo Kio PMD fire
sections.summary: In a PMD-related fire in an Ang Mo Kio flat last month, four people were rescued from a neighbouring flat and another 60 were evacuated.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: For example, in a PMD-related fire in a flat in Ang Mo Kio last month, four people had to be rescued from a neighbouring flat, while another 60 people were evacuated.

sections.label: HFAD scheme, audits, third-party officers
sections.summary: SCDF should extend the HFAD Assistance Scheme to HDB dwellers such as seniors in studio apartments and 2-room flats, and the Bill allows third-party officers with body cameras to conduct inspections.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Furthermore, SCDF should extend the HFAD Assistance Scheme to HDB dwellers, especially our senior citizens, who reside in studio apartments and 2-room flats.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The third issue is fire safety audit checks on HDB residential buildings.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: This Bill will allow authorised third-party officers to conduct routine fire safety and building inspections and these officers would wear body cameras and be subjected to SCDF audits.

sections.label: SCDF entry and investigative powers
sections.summary: The Bill strengthens SCDF investigative powers and lets officers enter any premises that may hold evidence linked to Fire Safety Act offences.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The fourth issue is regarding the powers of SCDF officers to enter into HDB flats to investigate and intervene in fire safety violations.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: This Bill will strengthen the SCDF's investigative powers and allow officers to enter any premises that may have evidence linked to the Fire Safety Act offences.

sections.label: Spike in PMD fires
sections.summary: The spike in PMD fires and related injuries is a timely reminder of the convergence of these trends.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The spike in PMD fires and injuries caused by the fires is a timely reminder of the convergence of these trends.

sections.label: Commissioner mandating fire safety upgrades
sections.summary: The Bill will empower the Commissioner to mandate building owners to install critical fire safety upgrades such as fire alarm systems.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The Bill will empower the Commissioner to mandate building owners to install critical fire safety upgrades, such as fire alarm systems.

sections.label: Fire injuries and HFADs
sections.summary: Fire injuries rose 50% from 60 in 2017 to 90 in 2018, all four 2018 fire fatalities were in HDB flats, and Minister Shanmugam said new and fire-safety-impacted residential units must install HFADs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Worryingly, there was a massive 50% increase in the number of fire injuries from 60 injuries in 2017 to 90 in 2018.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: All four fatalities caused by fire in 2018 also occurred in HDB flats.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Minister Shanmugam responded that all new residential units and residential units undergoing works which impact fire safety will be required to install HFADs.

sections.label: Kyoto Animation arson attack
sections.summary: The Kyoto Animation arson attack killed 35 employees in their 20s and 30s, and the building, exempted as a small office building, lacked fire sprinklers, indoor fire hose reels and protected staircases included in this Bill.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Last month, the Kyoto Animation arson attack in Japan tragically took 35 lives, all employees in their 20s and 30s.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The building had just passed a fire safety inspection in October last year, but as it was designated a small office building, it was exempted from installing fire sprinklers, indoor fire hose reels and protected staircases leading to external areas, all safety features which could have helped reduce the number of lives lost and which are, thankfully, included in this Bill.

sections.label: Compartmented rooms for healthcare buildings
sections.summary: The new regulations require at least two compartmented rooms for horizontal evacuation, but only for healthcare buildings primarily.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The new regulations require at least two compartmented rooms for horizontal evacuation, but only for healthcare buildings primarily.

sections.label: Punishing non-compliant product suppliers
sections.summary: Part V amendments empower SCDF to go upstream to punish suppliers of non-compliant products and building materials and ban their use.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The amendments which are specified in Part V of the Bill to empower SCDF to go upstream to punish suppliers which provide non-compliant products and building materials and ban their use is certainly a step in the right direction.

sections.label: Keeping free passage for emergency access
sections.summary: Residents need to be reminded that they must keep a 1.2-metre free passage for emergency access.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Residents need to be reminded that they must keep a 1.2-metre free passage for emergency access.

sections.label: SCDF outsourcing routine inspections
sections.summary: SCDF intends to outsource routine inspections and enforcement to authorised third parties to focus on higher fire risk areas.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: As SCDF wants to focus on higher fire risk areas, it intends to outsource routine inspections and enforcement to authorised third parties, such as retired Police Officers and other public servants.

sections.label: Elderly hoarding fire concerns
sections.summary: The speaker is concerned about more hoarding cases among older residents, with fires caused by flammable items hoarded by the elderly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I am concerned that we will face more cases of hoardings among older residents with our rapidly ageing population.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: There have been a number of fires due to the large quantities of flammable items hoarded by the elderly in their flats.

sections.label: Fire alarms in HDB areas
sections.summary: The speaker appeals to the Government to install and maintain fire alarm systems and sprinklers in all HDB estates, old and new.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The last point I would like to make is on the installation of fire alarm systems and sprinklers in our HDB common areas and neighbourhood shops.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I appeal to the Government to install and maintain these systems in all our HDB estates, old and new, as an additional safety measure and to minimise potential fire damage.

sections.label: Buildings needing fire safety upgrades
sections.summary: About 500 buildings would be required to undergo fire safety upgrades, some predating the 1991 Fire Code.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: As indicated by the Senior Parliamentary Secretary earlier, there are some 500 buildings that would be required to undergo such fire safety upgrades.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: These buildings have not undergone any A&A works for some time, and some predate even the 1991 Fire Code.

sections.label: NTU study on building numbers
sections.summary: A 2005 NTU study estimated close to 160,000 buildings in Singapore, as there is no official census.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: While there is no official census on the number of buildings in Singapore, a study done by the Nanyang Technological University (NTU) in 2005 estimated that there were close to 160,000 buildings in Singapore.

sections.label: PMD fire investigation patterns
sections.summary: The speaker asks if SCDF found useful patterns or early warning signs of high fire-risk PMDs from past PMD-related fire investigations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: From the investigation into the past PMD-related fires, I would like to ask if SCDF has found any useful patterns or any early warning signs of high fire-risk PMDs.

sections.label: Updating fire safety laws
sections.summary: The passage says fire safety laws must be regularly updated, and the proposed amendments will attend to some 500 old commercial and industrial buildings.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It is crucial that our fire safety laws are regularly updated to respond to the changing nature of fire safety risks and challenges, especially in light of the significant number of fires in the last month alone.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I understand that the proposed amendments will attend to some 500 old buildings that are mostly commercial and industrial.

sections.label: Fire incident numbers
sections.summary: The passage states that 2,411 fire incidents happened in 2018, while 515 fires took place in non-residential premises.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In addition, a total of 2,411 fire incidents happened in 2018.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In contrast, 515 fires took place in non-residential premises.

sections.label: Elderly fire risk groups
sections.summary: The passage states that fires are a particular risk for two vulnerable groups within the elderly segment, and 82,000 people live with dementia at home.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Fires are a particular risk for two vulnerable groups within the elderly segment.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: There are 82,000 people who live with dementia at home.

sections.label: Sprinklers and PMD fires
sections.summary: The passage states the Fire Code requires sprinklers in certain HDB areas, MND said SCDF saw no need for sprinklers in residential units, and asks if SCDF has a new position given 54 PMD fires.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Fire Code currently provides that sprinklers be placed in certain areas of HDB buildings.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: But in response to a Parliamentary Question posed in July 2018, the Ministry of National Development replied that “SCDF’s assessment at this point in time is that there is no need to install sprinklers within the residential units.” Is there now a new position on this by SCDF, especially considering the 54 fires involving PMDs in the first half of this year, a number that has more than doubled compared to the same period last year?

sections.label: Smoke alarm and extinguisher findings
sections.summary: The passage states fatal fire rates fell 46% in the US and 41% in Japan after smoke alarms were mandated, and 88% of fires tackled with extinguishers were put out.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In the US and Japan, after home smoke alarms were made mandatory in 1976 and 2006 respectively, the rate of fatal fire incidents have decreased by 46% in the US and 41% in Japan.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Britain’s Fire Industry Association also found that 88% of fires tackled with extinguishers were put out.

sections.label: Incentivising home fire equipment
sections.summary: The passage asks whether homeowners could be further incentivised to equip their homes with fire extinguishers and smoke alarms through discounts on conservancy charges or home fire insurance premiums.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: If mandating for all is not an option, can we consider further incentivising homeowners to equip their homes with fire extinguishers and smoke alarms through offering discounts for conservancy charges or discounts for home fire insurance premiums?

sections.label: Fire Safety Act penalties
sections.summary: The speaker notes dissimilar fire causes, warns against complacency, and welcomes harsher penalties for five Fire Safety Act offences.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: The causes of the fires across all three incidents were dissimilar and although no one was badly injured, scalded or perished, we should not be lulled into complacency and think that it will not happen to any of us, be it in our homes or at our offices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: I applaud the move in this Bill to introduce harsher and more deterrent penalties for five offences under the Fire Safety Act.

sections.label: SCDF enforcement and investigative powers
sections.summary: The speaker supports enhancing SCDF's enforcement and investigative powers to hold those who flout fire safety rules responsible.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: By the same token, I support the enhancement of SCDF’s enforcement and investigative powers to hold responsible those who flout fire safety rules.

sections.label: Immediate prosecution of culpable parties
sections.summary: The speaker supports SCDF having the option to immediately prosecute culpable parties in such cases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: In such cases, I am supportive that SCDF will now have the option to immediately prosecute culpable parties.

sections.label: Supply chain for fire safety products
sections.summary: The speaker notes e-commerce suppliers of fire extinguishers and that MHA will introduce measures to tighten control over the regulated fire safety products supply chain.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: These days, we have various suppliers, including many e-commerce sites hosted locally and abroad, peddling fire extinguishers and fire extinguishing devices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: I take cognisance of the fact that MHA will be introducing new measures to tighten control over the supply chain for regulated fire safety products.

sections.label: Fire Safety Bill key amendments
sections.summary: The Bill strengthens SCDF's regulatory and enforcement powers, and would require older and higher-risk buildings to install critical fire safety features.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: The key amendments of the Bill seek to enhance the fire safety of buildings by strengthening SCDF’s regulatory and enforcement powers to optimise the use of SCDF’s resources and to streamline regulatory processes for greater clarity.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: The Fire Safety Bill, with the tightened safety regulations and certification processes for buildings, if approved, will require older buildings, which have not undergone A&A as well as buildings where the occupants are at a higher risk in the event of a fire, to install critical fire safety features.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: This is in compliance with the latest Fire Code, and it has been pointed out that some 500 buildings in Singapore that were built before the 1001/2002 Fire Code and have a higher occupancy load, require these features.

sections.label: Third-party fire safety officers
sections.summary: Given manpower strain, the speaker understands the Bill seeks to empower SCDF to appoint authorised third-party officers for routine enforcement checks and building inspections.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: With the strain on manpower, I understand the rationale for the Bill to also seek to empower SCDF to appoint authorised third-party officers to conduct routine fire safety enforcement checks and building inspections.

sections.label: PMD fires in HDB flats
sections.summary: Asks the Minister for fire safety standards and measures for fire risks in HDB blocks and flats, given PMD fire incidents.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: With many Singaporeans living in HDB flats, and given the rise in PMD fire incidents within HDB flats and blocks, can the Minister also share the fire safety standards and measures to handle fire risks of HDB blocks and flats?

sections.label: Smoke alarms in rental flats
sections.summary: SCDF, HDB and PA install smoke alarms free in HDB Public Rental flats, covering over 50,000 households, prioritising those with a member aged 60 and above.

sentences.speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: SCDF, HDB and the People's Association (PA) have also been working together to install smoke alarms in flats let out under the HDB Public Rental scheme at no additional cost to tenants.

sentences.speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: More than 50,000 households will be covered by this assistance scheme, and installations implemented in phases to prioritise households with one member aged 60 and above.

sections.label: Residential fire calls and casualties
sections.summary: Of 4,114 fire calls in 2016, 68.5% were residential, up 62.9% from 2015, with deaths and injuries in 2016 and 2017.

sentences.speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Out of the 4,114 fire calls responded to in 2016 in Singapore, 68.5% were fires in residential areas, an increase of 62.9% compared to 2015.

sentences.speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: These fire incidents have resulted in three deaths and 60 injured in 2017, two deaths and 62 injured in 2016.

sections.label: Bill on building fire safety
sections.summary: The Bill empowers SCDF to require building owners to install critical fire safety features, as over 2,000 residential fires occur yearly, about half rubbish chute fires.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The Bill seeks to enhance the fire safety of buildings by empowering SCDF to require building owners to install critical fire safety features, such as protected exit staircases and fire alarm systems.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Every year, over 2,000 fires break out in residences, with about half being rubbish chute fires.

sections.label: HFAD installation in flats
sections.summary: Notes Government is installing HFAD in all HDB Public Rental flats and that HFAD installation is mandatory for new residences and existing premises doing fire safety works.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I hope the Ministry would consider ways to protect this vulnerable group of residents.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I am aware that the Government is installing HFAD in all HDB Public Rental flats and the installation of HFADs is mandatory for new residences and existing residential premises carrying out fire safety works.

sections.label: PMD trade-in scheme proposal
sections.summary: Urges the Ministry to work with MOT on a national scheme letting PMD owners trade in unapproved models for approved ones, for fire safety.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: A recent spate of fires caused by PMDs has drawn our attention to the risks of these machines, so much so that PMD fires are fast becoming a new fire risk category.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I urge the Ministry to work with MOT to implement a national scheme to allow PMD owners to trade in their unapproved models earlier for the approved ones, in consideration of fire safety.

sections.label: SCDF powers over fire safety products
sections.summary: Amendments give SCDF power to require testing and rectification of non-compliant fire safety products, including cladding samples from project sites.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: With the proposed amendments, in addition to non-renewal of the Fire Certificates, SCDF will have the power to require regulated fire safety products to be tested and for rectification action to be taken for use of non-compliant products.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: For example, SCDF will henceforth require samples of cladding from each project site to be tested, over and above the current annual tests conducted on samples obtained from the warehouses.

sections.label: SCDF inspections and third-party officers
sections.summary: SCDF will keep issuing composition notices and fines until about five third-party officers are competent, covering roughly 2,000 inspections yearly.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: As I have mentioned in my earlier speech, there are about 2,000 such inspections annually.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Until we are confident that these officers are competent in their duties, SCDF will continue to issue composition notices and collect fines.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: And as I mentioned earlier, SCDF is looking to start with a small team of around five third-party officers.

sections.label: Compliance timeframes for building owners
sections.summary: SCDF will assess compliance timeframes case by case, allow up to two years, consider extensions, and may waive requirements for imminent sale or redevelopment.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: SCDF will work with the building owners to assess the timeframe for compliance on a case-by-case basis and are prepared to give building owners up to two years to comply with the requirements.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: SCDF is also prepared to exercise flexibility to help the building owners meet the requirements.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: If more time is required, building owners may also request for a timeline extension and, if there is a definite plan for sale or redevelopment in the immediate future, SCDF may consider waiving the requirements.

sections.label: Public extinguishing fires in 2018
sections.summary: In 2018, about 25% of such fires were successfully extinguished by alert members of the public.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: In fact, such fires can be easily put out by members of the public.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: I am heartened to share that in 2018, about 25% of such fires were successfully extinguished by alert members of the public.

sections.label: Definition of public building amended
sections.summary: The definition of public building will be amended to refer to any building the public or a section of the public may access.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: As Mr Christopher de Souza has highlighted, the definition of "public building" will be amended to refer to any building to which access to the public or a section of the public is allowed.

sections.label: Residential fire and fatality decline
sections.summary: Residential fires fell about 14.5% over three years, with fatalities halved from 0.15 per 100,000 in 2014 to 0.07 in 2018.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: The number of fires at residential premises has decreased by about 14.5% over the past three years.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: We have succeeded in reducing it by half, from 0.15 fatalities per 100,000 population in 2014, to 0.07 in 2018.

sections.label: False fire alarm activations
sections.summary: SCDF records show about 47,000 alarm activations yearly in buildings with central fire alarm systems, with under 1% involving real fires.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: To give Members a sense of the potential challenge that we will face with false alarms, SCDF's records showed that for buildings with central fire alarm systems now, there were about 47,000 alarm activations per year, out of which, less than 1% involved a real fire.

sections.label: Existing flat HFAD installation
sections.summary: Installing in existing flats needs flat dwellers' permission, and 12,000 households took up installation after one year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Installation in existing flats requires the permission of flat dwellers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: So far, 12,000 households have taken up the installation after one year of implementation.

sections.label: Visual alert HFADs
sections.summary: These households will be provided with HFADs that give visual alerts instead.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: To cater to their needs, we will provide these households with HFADs that give visual alerts instead.

sections.label: PMD fire safety measures
sections.summary: MOT and LTA plans bring forward UL-2272 compliance to 1 July 2020, with incentives for replacing non-certified PMDs and fire safety habit advice.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: As I have briefly mentioned earlier, the Senior Minister of State for Transport had spoken about MOT's and LTA's plans to bring forward the deadline for compliance with UL-2272 standard to 1 July 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: MOT is also planning for incentives to encourage the replacement and disposal of non-certified PMDs which have been found to be involved in most, if not all, of the recent spate of PMD fires.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: As for what PMD owners can do to prevent fires, we encourage users to adopt good fire safety habits, such as regularly inspecting batteries for signs of damage and corrosion and to avoid leaving charging devices unattended for an extended period of time.

sections.label: myResponder app registrations
sections.summary: Registrations on the myResponder app increased over the years, going up by 75% in 2018.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Mr Christopher de Souza asked about the myResponder app.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: I am pleased to share that the number of registrations on the myResponder app has increased over the years, going up by 75% in 2018.

sections.label: MHA fire safety approach
sections.summary: MHA and SCDF will study them and work with agencies and stakeholders to keep fire safety measures effective, continuing a multi-pronged approach.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: MHA and SCDF will study them carefully and work with relevant agencies and stakeholders to ensure the continued effectiveness of our fire safety measures that will keep our public safe.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: MHA will continue with our multi-pronged approach to fire safety.

sections.label: HFAD installation in rental flats
sections.summary: HFADs have been installed for about a year, reaching about 12,000 of 60,000 rental flats, with permission needed for existing households and possible scheme expansion to be studied.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: As I mentioned in my speech, we have already started the installation of HFADs for public rental flats.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: We have done this for about a year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: We have a stock supply of about 60,000 rental flats.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: After a year of implementation, we are now at about 12,000 households.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: But when we are looking at existing households, we have to seek permission to enter the home to install the HFADs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: So, like I mentioned in my speech, we will study the need to expand the existing scheme to broader groups of families.
